title: The Saint of Static
hook: An old community radio frequency begins broadcasting confessions from people who are still alive and have not said the words yet.
truth: A dead emergency broadcaster has become a signal-haunt that feeds on confession, shame, and electrical attention.

monster.name: The Saint of Static
monster.instinct: To make every private sin public and gather worship through interference.
weaknesses: grounded copper from the original transmitter
a true confession freely given and then forgiven

countdown.label: First Sign
countdown.text: A dead frequency interrupts car radios with a calm voice naming streets and regrets.

countdown.label: First Harm
countdown.text: A city councillor hears their own future confession and panics on camera.

countdown.label: Spread
countdown.text: Phone speakers begin using the voices of missing relatives.

countdown.label: Gathering
countdown.text: Listeners gather under an obsolete transmission mast and answer the broadcast in unison.

countdown.label: Breakdown
countdown.text: A rolling blackout leaves only the haunted frequency alive.

countdown.label: Finale
countdown.text: The Saint speaks through every device in the city and asks for one final confession.

clues.text: The same obsolete call sign is scratched into three different radio cabinets.
A printed transcript contains a conversation scheduled for tomorrow.
Ground wires near the old mast are burned through from the inside.
The signal cannot cross eight seconds of intentional silence.
One recorded confession loses its static after the harmed person forgives the speaker.
A radio station archive fire killed an emergency broadcaster during a storm evacuation.

keeperHints: Let devices become intimate before they become dangerous.
The Saint should sound kind, patient, and absolutely invasive.
Use silence as a meaningful tool, not just an absence of sound.
revealPolicy: Do not make the broadcast omniscient immediately; let it overreach and expose its limits.
automationSafety: Do not invent humiliating secrets for player characters without consent.
When a confession is needed, offer pressure and choices rather than declaring one.
